svg.title: Word vectors: factorization and nearest neighbours
svg.desc: Rank-24 vectors from five orthogonal iterations over the PPMI matrix, and the five nearest vocabulary words of eight probe words by cosine similarity.
svg.text: WORD VECTORS -- rank-24 by orthogonal iteration, nearest neighbours
WHAT: Q = orthonormalize(random [V, 24]); repeat five times Q = orthonormalize(P Q); vectors = rows of P Q, unit length.
switches: toggle speed opening indicator lights
glyphs: not in the vocabulary (seen fewer than twice)
disk: desk load unlock console file
jupiter: galileo orbiter spacecraft including hubble
apl: cor24 uart lisp comparison forth
router: expert token fits per stores
WHY: orthogonal iteration is power iteration for several vectors at once; with Gram-Schmidt between steps the columns
converge to the leading eigenvectors of the symmetric PPMI matrix, the same subspace a truncated SVD would give.
HOW: u:wv_orthonormalize is Gram-Schmidt over columns (concat on axis 1); u:wv_factor multiplies by P and re-orthonormalizes;
u:wv_neighbours ranks cosine similarities with argtop_k, the word itself excluded. Everything is deterministic (seeded).
WHY IT MAY NOT BE ENOUGH: a few thousand tokens give noisy neighbours; words seen once have no vector at all, and
hashing 586 words into 1,024 rows makes some share a row. The paraphrase columns decide, not the neighbour lists.
Numbers: docent results table rows CD01b (fine-tuned) and CD01bf (frozen) beside CD01, MB01, and MB01t.
